claim: The byte beside this type's manual is the gain of a feedback loop closed around the all-pass cascade, and it is not a second mix and not a resonance inside the sections. A cascade passes everything at unit gain, so summing it with the dry signal reaches six decibels where the two arrive in phase and no further; the profile reaches 18.87 dB, which a sum would need nearly eight helpings of the cascade to do. What the loop puts there instead is a resonance between each pair of notches -- where the cascade comes back in phase with itself and the return adds up -- while the notches stay where the closed reading put them. Two further things about it are readable, one at each end of the band. The return arrives one sample late, which is what a part computing a sample at a time has no choice about, and the phase that costs is nothing at the bottom and half a circle at half the rate: at the top of the band it turns the highest resonance into the cancellation it would otherwise have been, which the unit does and an instantaneous loop does not. And the return will not carry the bottom of the band: the lowest resonance is largest at 105 Hz and has fallen thirteen decibels by 25, by more the harder the loop is driven and by nothing at all when the loop is open -- which puts one pole of a high pass inside the loop and nowhere else in the chain. The loop gains themselves are a readout of seventeen settings and no law is claimed on them. What the seventeen do settle is that there is something to claim: the gain moves at every one of them, and the two that share the top four bits of the byte come back 0.0675 apart -- further than any neighbouring pair of the sweep -- so this byte is not the sixteen-entry table the byte one address along on the same type turned out to be.
named: a feedback path around an all-pass cascade, a sample late and blocked at DC
adds: The two records say what this byte did to each twelfth-octave band at three settings, once with the type's mix at the top of its range and once at its middle. What is read out of them here is that the byte is a loop rather than a mix or a section resonance, where the loop is closed, that its return is a sample late, and that it does not pass the bottom of the band. The records name no loop, no delay and no filter, and say so.
refutedBy: A setting of this byte that raised the profile without putting a resonance between the notches, or one that moved a notch, either of which would make the byte something other than a loop gain. Or the top band coming back where an instantaneous loop puts it on a second run, which would take the sample of delay away. Or the shortfall at the bottom of the band turning out not to follow the loop gain, which would move the high pass out of the return path.

eraPriors.claim: A loop computed a sample at a time returns the previous result, because the present one is what is being computed. A delay of one sample is therefore not a refinement on the loop but the only form it can take.
eraPriors.why: It is the difference between a loop that can be written and one that cannot, and it is readable rather than assumed: the phase it costs grows with frequency and is worth a whole half circle at half the rate, so the two readings disagree by eighteen decibels in the top band and by nothing over the rest.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The top band came back where an instantaneous loop puts it. The reading is at the edge of the band set and a single band wide, so it is the one figure here a second run could most easily overturn -- and if it did, the loop would have to be reached some other way than sample by sample.

eraPriors.claim: A fixed-point loop that passes DC accumulates the offset its arithmetic cannot represent, so a part that closes one puts a pole of a high pass in the return path and puts its corner as low as it can.
eraPriors.why: It says where the filter is rather than that there is one, and that is the part the measurement answers: a filter anywhere outside the loop would cut the bottom of the band by the same amount at every setting, and what the record shows is a shortfall that is nothing with the loop open and thirteen decibels with it nearly closed.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The shortfall at the bottom of the band did not follow the loop gain. A constant one would put the filter in the signal path, and none at all would leave the loop flat to nothing -- which for a fixed-point part would be the more surprising of the two.

alternatives.reading: The cascade is four second-order all-pass sections rather than eight first-order ones, with this byte as the loop gain either way.
The loop gain runs on a law in the byte rather than on the three numbers published here.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Half of it. The sweep was made and the byte is neither of the two things three points left open: not a straight line, which the middle setting already said and the seventeen now say in one direction at every setting between the ends; and not a table of sixteen read through the byte's top four bits, because 120 and 127 share those four bits and come back 0.0675 apart. What it is instead is one setting short of answerable and is the alternative below.

alternatives.reading: The byte adds more of the cascade to the dry signal, on top of what the mix byte already added.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Arithmetic, with no fit needed and none possible here. A cascade of all-pass sections passes every frequency at unit gain, so a sum of it with the dry reaches 20 log10(1 + mix) where the two arrive in phase. The profile reaches 18.87 dB, which needs 7.78 helpings of it -- and the type's mix byte was already held at the top of its printed range. It is not in the ranking because this harness renders every model's flat reference from the same byte block with the swept address at nothing, so a candidate that moves the mix onto the swept address renders its own flat reference at that mix and reports no deviation at all at the setting of zero. That is a property of the harness rather than of the reading, and saying so is why the arithmetic is quoted instead of a score.

alternatives.reading: The byte is the resonance of the all-pass sections themselves, which is where four second-order sections would differ from eight first-order ones.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Its own direction. An all-pass has unit magnitude at every resonance, so raising one moves notches and cannot raise a profile anywhere; scored against these records the best resonance it can find goes down as the byte goes up -- 0.4992593313618718, 0.4481299101573052, 0.39000961388318234 -- which is the sections getting shallower rather than sharper. At the setting where the byte is nothing it returns a half, which is the first-order cascade exactly, and that is the only setting it fits.

alternatives.reading: The gain is a table of sixteen entries with the byte's low three bits interpolating between them, rather than a law computed from the whole byte.

gates.why: The three things claimed are read in three places and each competing reading fails in its own. Taking the sample of delay out puts the worst band at 14254 Hz, the top of the set, where the model has a cancellation and the unit has a resonance -- 18.2 dB out. Taking the blocked return out puts it at 26.3 Hz, the bottom, where the model has a resonance and the unit has almost none -- 12.8 dB. Closing the loop around the summed output instead fills the first notch in and is 20.1 dB out at 1887.7 Hz, which is where the notch is. Closing it around four of the eight sections puts resonances at twice the spacing and lands one on top of a notch, 25.9 dB out at 6349.6 Hz. None of these is a fit that is merely worse: each is a feature in the wrong place.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// roland-sc8850-01  ·  01 20  ·  phaser-resonance
//
// Generated by yarn sync from inferences/models/0120-a-loop-a-sample-late-through-a-blocked-return.json.
// The claim it closes: inferences/roland-sc8850-01/0120-the-resonance-byte-closes-a-loop.json
//
// Every constant, every section count and every structural choice below is
// the model's. The difference equations are the ordinary realisations of the
// sections the model names — this site's arithmetic, not a measurement.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#include <cmath>

namespace soundings::roland_sc8850_01::type_01_20 {

// Carried from the claim that measured it. The rate is not refitted here and could not be:
// what this byte adds to the profile is read against notches whose places the closed
// reading already fixed.
constexpr double kSampleRateHz = 32000.0;
constexpr double kPi = 3.14159265358979323846;

/**
 * One first-order all-pass section: unit gain at every frequency, and a phase
 * that runs from nothing to half a turn through the corner. Bilinear-transformed,
 * so the corner is prewarped and sits where it is asked for.
 */
struct Allpass1 {
  double a = 0.0, x1 = 0.0, y1 = 0.0;

  void setCornerHz(double hz) {
    const double k = std::tan(kPi * hz / kSampleRateHz);
    a = (k - 1.0) / (k + 1.0);
  }

  double process(double x) {
    const double y = a * x + x1 - a * y1;
    x1 = x;
    y1 = y;
    return y;
  }
};

/** A one-pole high-pass, which is what blocking a loop at DC comes to. */
struct DcBlock {
  double r = 0.0, x1 = 0.0, y1 = 0.0;

  void setCornerHz(double hz) { r = std::exp(-2.0 * kPi * hz / kSampleRateHz); }

  double process(double x) {
    const double y = x - x1 + r * y1;
    x1 = x;
    y1 = y;
    return y;
  }
};

// 22 settings read, interpolated in log between them and flat outside them
// read from data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-bands/01-20-03-where-the-phaser-sits-in-twelfths.json
inline double allpassChain0CornerHz(int byte) {
  static const int kAt[] = {0, 7, 8, 12, 15, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 63, 64, 72, 80, 88, 96, 104, 112, 114, 120, 127};
  static const double kRead[] = {1040.20537551, 1382.24867349, 1437.04744609, 1626.57375789, 1778.28049374, 1824.17100715, 2395.9684461, 3097.9436758, 3816.53602885, 4485.52633619, 5378.2567592, 7488.34309768, 7803.0377261, 9356.45582284, 10504.5321755, 11354.2965806, 12102.9125491, 12514.7412616, 12962.003096, 13092.7790669, 13345.8540008, 13508.3953318};
  constexpr int kCount = sizeof(kAt) / sizeof(kAt[0]);
  if (byte <= kAt[0]) return kRead[0];
  if (byte >= kAt[kCount - 1]) return kRead[kCount - 1];
  int i = 1;
  while (kAt[i] < byte) ++i;
  const double t = static_cast<double>(byte - kAt[i - 1]) / (kAt[i] - kAt[i - 1]);
  // The settings were read an octave or so apart, so what sits between two of
  // them is their geometric mean and not their arithmetic one.
  return std::exp(std::log(kRead[i - 1]) + t * (std::log(kRead[i]) - std::log(kRead[i - 1])));
}

// 2 settings read, interpolated linearly between them and flat outside them
inline double allpassChain0Mix(int byte) {
  static const int kAt[] = {0, 127};
  static const double kRead[] = {0.0, 1.0};
  constexpr int kCount = sizeof(kAt) / sizeof(kAt[0]);
  if (byte <= kAt[0]) return kRead[0];
  if (byte >= kAt[kCount - 1]) return kRead[kCount - 1];
  int i = 1;
  while (kAt[i] < byte) ++i;
  const double t = static_cast<double>(byte - kAt[i - 1]) / (kAt[i] - kAt[i - 1]);
  return kRead[i - 1] + t * (kRead[i] - kRead[i - 1]);
}

// 17 settings read, interpolated linearly between them and flat outside them
// read from data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-bands/01-20-06-the-resonance-between-the-three-in-twelfths.json
inline double allpassChain0Feedback(int byte) {
  static const int kAt[] = {0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80, 88, 96, 104, 112, 120, 127};
  static const double kRead[] = {0.0, 0.0375, 0.075, 0.11, 0.165, 0.2125, 0.255, 0.315, 0.37, 0.43, 0.465, 0.53, 0.61, 0.6725, 0.74, 0.8175, 0.885};
  constexpr int kCount = sizeof(kAt) / sizeof(kAt[0]);
  if (byte <= kAt[0]) return kRead[0];
  if (byte >= kAt[kCount - 1]) return kRead[kCount - 1];
  int i = 1;
  while (kAt[i] < byte) ++i;
  const double t = static_cast<double>(byte - kAt[i - 1]) / (kAt[i] - kAt[i - 1]);
  return kRead[i - 1] + t * (kRead[i] - kRead[i - 1]);
}

/** The chain the model names, in the order it names it. */
struct Effect {
  Allpass1 allpass0[8];
  double mix0 = 0.0;
  double feedback0 = 0.0;
  double loop0 = 0.0;
  DcBlock block0;

  void prepare(int b40_03_03, int b40_03_07, int b40_03_06) {
    const double corner0 = allpassChain0CornerHz(b40_03_03);
    for (Allpass1& section : allpass0) section.setCornerHz(corner0);
    mix0 = allpassChain0Mix(b40_03_07);
    feedback0 = allpassChain0Feedback(b40_03_06);
    block0.setCornerHz(20.0);
  }

  double process(double x) {
    // The loop returns one sample late and through a block at DC, which is what
    // the model names. The cascade is summed with the dry, never averaged with it.
    double wet0 = x + feedback0 * block0.process(loop0);
    for (Allpass1& section : allpass0) wet0 = section.process(wet0);
    loop0 = wet0;
    x = x + mix0 * wet0;
    return x;
  }
};
